children: Commodity markets traded mixed on September 10, with oil prices holding firm after Brent crude breached the $100-a-barrel mark, while gold prices steadied as investors awaited US inflation data due later this week.

Oil prices held firm on Thursday after Brent crude breached $100 a barrel, with traders bracing for deeper supply disruption as Iran and the United States launched their largest attacks on shipping since their six-month-old conflict began.
Brent crude futures rose 0.1% to $101.34 a barrel. U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude was at $96.55 a barrel, up 0.5%.
Gold steadied, as traders awaited US inflation data due later this week for clues to whether the Federal Reserve will hike interest rates.
Bullion was near $4,400 an ounce, after adding 1% in the previous session to snap a three-day losing streak.
Among other precious metals, silver was little changed at $67.29 an ounce, after adding 2.4% in the previous session. Platinum and palladium edged higher.
The dollar index was little changed against the other major currencies in the early Thursday trade.

title: Commodity Corner: Brent crude breaches $100/bbl on supply concerns; gold steady ahead of US inflation data
